name: Understanding how models process language internally
gist: These papers study how models work internally—looking at attention patterns, hidden representations, and activation steering to improve performance and explain behavior.
explain: Language models work by processing text through layers of neural networks, where information flows through billions of parameters and computations happen inside a black box. Papers in this area open the black box by studying attention patterns—which words the model focuses on when processing each token—and hidden representations—what patterns the model has learned to recognize at each layer. Some papers use neuron-steering, where researchers modify what individual neurons are computing mid-process to change the final output, which reveals what each neuron controls. The goal is to understand how models work and use that understanding to improve them, because you cannot fix systems you do not understand.

The challenge is that billions of parameters make it hard to figure out which ones matter for specific behaviors. A single neuron rarely does one thing—its behavior emerges from complex interactions. Papers study this by looking at examples: for a specific task, which patterns of neuron-firing appear? Do attention patterns make intuitive sense? Can you predict what a model will do based on its internal states? Some papers do ablation studies where they remove or modify specific components and measure the impact. The work is technically difficult because you need careful experimental design to isolate causation from correlation.

The payoff is that understanding internals enables better design because precise knowledge beats guessing. If you know that a model is using an attention pattern that makes sense but is slightly wrong, you can try to steer it toward better patterns by nudging the neurons, which improves performance surgically because you target the real problem. If you discover that certain layers are redundant, you can remove them to save computation. Some papers find that models learn interpretable features—like individual neurons that respond to specific concepts—which helps with debugging because you know what went wrong, and with safety because you can predict failure modes. This research area also answers scientific questions about what it takes for a system to learn language patterns, which has implications for understanding biological brains because the same principles might apply.

papers.title: DSSA: Dense-Sparse Switchable Attention for Seamless Short-to-Long Adaptation
papers.contribution: DSSA achieves 4x speedup over dense attention while retaining 98.1% performance on long-context understanding and 99.7% on chain-of-thought reasoning.

papers.title: Draft-based Approximate Inference for LLMs
papers.contribution: SpecKV and SpecPC methods consistently achieve higher accuracy than baselines while maintaining the same efficiency gains in memory and latency.

papers.title: LLM Pretraining with Continuous Concepts
papers.contribution: Outperforms standard next token prediction and knowledge distillation on benchmarks with improved sample efficiency and enhanced interpretability.

papers.title: The First Impression Problem: Internal Bias Triggers Overthinking in Reasoning Models
papers.contribution: Demonstrates causal relationship between internal bias and overthinking across multiple reasoning models and tasks, though mitigation methods remain ineffective.

papers.title: Universal Properties of Activation Sparsity in Modern Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Results uncover universal properties of activation sparsity across diverse models and scales, showing potential for effective sparsity grows with model size, with first study of activation sparsity in diffusion-based LLMs.

papers.title: Activation Steering with a Feedback Controller
papers.contribution: PID Steering consistently outperforms existing approaches across LLM families and benchmarks, achieving more robust and reliable behavioral control.

papers.title: AdaRoPE: Not All Attention Heads Should Rotate and Scale Equally
papers.contribution: Pretrained LLMs with AdaRoPE consistently outperform existing RoPE variants and enable better context extension while preserving short-context performance.

papers.title: Beyond Magic Words: Sharpness-Aware Prompt Evolving for Robust Large Language Models with TARE
papers.contribution: Generates prompts that preserve accuracy under paraphrasing; ATARE adapts with anisotropic weights and balances exploration-fidelity, outperforming accuracy-only prompt search.

papers.title: CLUE: Conflict-guided Localization for LLM Unlearning Framework
papers.contribution: Achieves superior forget efficacy and retain utility through precise neural localization compared to existing localization methods.

papers.title: Decoupling The "What" and "Where" With Polar Coordinate Positional Embedding
papers.contribution: Superior performance on diagnostic tasks and autoregressive modeling across music, genomic, and language domains; strong zero-shot length extrapolation capabilities.

papers.title: Enhancing Instruction Following of LLMs via Activation Steering with Dynamic Rejection
papers.contribution: Significantly enhances instruction-following capabilities across diverse benchmarks with up to 6.5% accuracy improvement over baselines without trade-offs in generation quality or task fidelity.

papers.title: FiX: Introducing Fine-grained Forget Gate into Softmax Attention
papers.contribution: FiX achieves lower training loss and superior performance on short-text benchmarks and long-context tasks compared to scalar-gate approaches.

papers.title: Fine-Grained Activation Steering: Steering Less, Achieving More
papers.contribution: AUSteer achieves more precise and effective steering than block-level approaches across multiple LLMs and tasks.

papers.title: KAST-BAR: Knowledge-Anchored Semantically-Dynamic Topology Brain Autoregressive Modeling for Universal Neural Interpretation
papers.contribution: KAST-BAR achieves state-of-the-art performance across six downstream tasks through large-scale pre-training on 21 diverse EEG datasets.

papers.title: Local Linearity of LLMs Enables Activation Steering via Model-Based Linear Optimal Control
papers.contribution: Achieves robust fine-grained behavior control with formal guarantees on steering performance; surpasses baseline methods for toxicity, truthfulness, refusal, and concept modulation.

papers.title: Log-Linear Attention
papers.contribution: Log-linear variants of Mamba-2 and Gated DeltaNet perform well compared to their linear-time counterparts while improving over baseline linear attention.

papers.title: Long-Context Generalization with Sparse Attention
papers.contribution: ASEntmax achieves up to 1000x length extrapolation on synthetic benchmarks and superior long-context generalization on language modeling while preserving short-context performance.

papers.title: ProxyAttn: Guided Sparse Attention via Representative Heads
papers.contribution: ProxyAttn achieves up to 10.3x attention acceleration and 2.4x prefilling acceleration without significant performance loss.

papers.contribution: Sparse Feature Attention matches dense baselines while improving speed 2.5x and reducing FLOPs and KV-cache by 50%; preserves retrieval accuracy at long contexts.

papers.title: Understanding and Improving Length Generalization in Hierarchical Sparse Attention Models
papers.contribution: Establishes new state-of-the-art for training-free length extrapolation: generalizes 4K-trained models to 32 million tokens on RULER and BABILong.

papers.title: Understanding the Ability of LLMs to Handle Character-Level Perturbation
papers.contribution: Reveals that LLMs maintain notable performance even under severe perturbations, unveiling architectural strengths and potential misuse risks.
